pr.title: Verify contained Jenkins sequential execution parity
pr.body:
Adds a reproducible, contained comparison between pinned Jenkins and the actual McLoving controller/agent for the existing sequential fixture contract. The fresh paired run found no unexplained differences across 10 authored positive fixtures plus C052, with 19 shell executions per runtime; 12 negative inputs produced no product work. All 23 inputs were compiled twice and independently replayed through Rust admission.

The separate 228-case original corpus classified as **1 admitted, 216 unsupported, 11 rejected, zero unverified** (226 exact originals and two previously retained redacted representations). These classification results do not claim execution parity for that corpus or production authority.

The change retains raw observations, pinned source recovery and offline verification, and wires the retained-evidence gate into Foundation. It also fixes the campaign launcher’s initialization/cleanup defects and the verifier’s stage-body tag attribution, preserving earlier failed attempts separately. JCOMP-002C closure is backed by its protected merge and successful exact-main Foundation/native Windows runs; JCOMP-003 remains ACTIVE pending its own protected merge and exact-main verification.

Validation: fresh compiler/admission build, 46 actual compiler validations, contained Jenkins and product execution with verified cleanup, all 228 genuine Rust admission replays, and independent recomputation of the paired report. Executed source is `f263ad4ae2871e8bb06fe3b5bceef534179a0a88`, tree `f49d17fe0c8e552e7968c83a153153a2fd777e54`, based on verified main `01137b54b8fbefdc0deb0214a5d4d8979a773575`. Later publication files do not relabel that execution source.

Paired report SHA-256: `b19894eaa818636f670d99a079e83c8dd12b5f6f6defc2cb0cd790e468c2fc6f`. Corpus campaign SHA-256: `0332856ee84aa5035dd65a2ad36bb5c83d17c4f88a77eaad99b37ce67ab20592`.
